evidence: Run 33437018488 failed Ubuntu x64 at the valid ahead branch check while macOS ARM64 passed the same commit.
Run 32462048454 failed the valid level branch check; run 32077308781 failed the valid rebased branch check; run 31942073162 failed the valid ahead branch check.
Before the fix, worktree.py ran git fetch through the bounded process owner without disabling automatic maintenance; Git documents post-fetch automatic maintenance as enabled by default.

Existing resolved records hermetic-git-fixture-processes and hermetic-git-fixture-coverage prove background Git maintenance already caused the same Linux CI boundary failure in two other fixture owners.
Git 2.28 documents --no-auto-gc; Git 2.29 and later document it as the compatibility synonym for --no-auto-maintenance; the installed Git 2.55 accepts the maintenance-free dry-run fetch.

The worktree readiness regression now asserts the exact maintenance-free fetch and passes level, ahead, diverged, and rebased branch cases; the project-gate regression, focused Pyright, Ruff format, and Ruff lint also pass.
failure: GitHub Actions intermittently rejects valid level, ahead, or rebased fixture branches in the worktree readiness contract, blocking the full gate and automatic release.
root_cause: The publish-readiness fetch allowed Git automatic maintenance to start after a successful fetch. The bounded runner correctly treats a remaining background process as failure, so the valid branch check was rejected at whichever fetch happened to trigger maintenance.
